title: Function Expressions Check
description: Expressions as values, calling after assignment, and hoisting differences.

questions.explanation: `double(5)` returns 10. A function expression stored in a variable has `typeof` `"function"`.
`const` bindings are not usable before their line. Function declarations hoist; expressions assigned with `const` do not.

options.text: Throws — cannot pass a function expression

questions.explanation: Expressions are values. Passing `triple` into `apply` calls it with `4` → `12`.
5 stays in range; -1 clamps to min 0. Same early-return logic as a declaration, stored as an expression.

options.text: `const f = function () {}` stores a function value; call only after that line runs
Function expressions hoist and can be called anywhere in the file
You cannot pass a function expression to another function
`typeof` of a function expression is always `"object"`

questions.explanation: Expressions are values bound by `const`/`let`. They are not declaration-style hoisted; `typeof` is `"function"`.
